articles.title: Discriminação política no trabalho: entenda o que diz a legislação | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo especialista, a Constituição Federal de 1988 proíbe privar pessoas de direitos por convicção política e veda qualquer forma de discriminação no acesso ao emprego. Neste ano, o MPT-go recebeu quase 60 denúncias de assédio eleitoral.
articles.summary: Segundo especialista, a Constituição Federal de 1988 proíbe privar pessoas de direitos por convicção política e veda qualquer forma de discriminação no acesso ao emprego.
articles.body:
Após o resultado das Eleições, que deu vitória ao presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), a psicóloga Mara Suassuna publicou um vídeo nas redes sociais em que falou sobre não selecionar petistas para vagas de emprego em sua empresa de recursos humanos. Diante disso, o g1 falou com especialistas para entender a legislação que proíbe esse e outros tipos de discriminação no contexto do trabalho.

No vídeo publicado pela psicóloga, ela diz que recebeu telefones de empresários que contratam seus serviços, pedindo para que ela selecionasse novos colaboradores com o critério de "não serem petistas" .

Em nota, Suassuna afirmou que fundamentou sua declaração na teoria desenvolvida pelo psicólogo Shalom H. Schwartz, que fala sobre valores básicos do ser humano e como isso orienta escolhas de comportamento (confira a nota completa ao final do texto) .

Ao g1 , o advogado Sebastião Justo, especialista em Direito do Trabalho e presidente da OAB Aparecida de Goiânia , que os artigos 5º e 7º da Constituição Federal de 1988 proíbem privar pessoas de direitos por convicção política e vedam qualquer forma de discriminação no acesso ao emprego.

Ele explica que a empresa deve se ater às características do candidato que serão essenciais para que a função descrita na vaga seja executada. Com isso, qualquer outro ponto analisado que não tenha relação com o trabalho não deve fazer parte da avaliação.

"A empresa pode avaliar tudo o que diz respeito à função: formação, experiência, competências técnicas e comportamentais, disponibilidade, adequação ao cargo. O limite é o critério que nada tem a ver com o trabalho. Voto, partido, religião, orientação sexual, estado civil, gravidez, situação de crédito: nada disso pode entrar na avaliação", afirmou.

Mara Suassuna é psicóloga e tem uma empresa de recrutamento profissional — Foto: Reprodução/Redes socias de Mara Suassuma

Além da Constituição, que é a base para a proteção, Justo também destaca a Lei 9.029/1995 , que proíbe a prática discriminatória para acesso ou manutenção da relação de emprego , e C onvenção nº 111 da Organização Internacional do Trabalho (OIT) , ratificada pelo Brasil, que define discriminação como toda distinção, exclusão ou preferência fundada, entre outros motivos, em opinião política.

"Uma declaração pública de que determinado grupo não será selecionado é, do ponto de vista jurídico, uma confissão antecipada de critério discriminatório. Ela vira prova em qualquer ação futura, inclusive contra as empresas que contratarem esse serviço de recrutamento, porque a responsabilidade por discriminação na seleção é de quem contrata, não só de quem seleciona", destacou.

De acordo com o advogado, o Ministério Público do Trabalho (MPT) recebeu cerca de 219 denúncias de assédio eleitoral em 2018 e cerca de 3,4 mil em 2022 .

Ao g1 , o MPT-GO informou que foram registradas 42 denúncias após o 1º turno e 15 após o 2º turno. As denúncias estão sob sigilo.

Para casos de discriminação, o advogado explica que a legislação prevê multa administrativa dez vezes maior que o salário pago pela empresa, que deve ser dobrada em caso de reincidência, e proibição de obter empréstimos e financiamentos em instituições financeiras oficiais.

Em caso de dispensa discriminatória, o trabalhador pode optar entre a reintegração com pagamento de todo o período de afastamento ou o recebimento em dobro dessas remunerações, sempre com correção e juros. A lei não exige motivo para dispensar, mas o motivo não pode ser ilícito, segundo o advogado.

"Se o trabalhador tem indícios de que foi demitido pela posição política, o primeiro passo é guardar as provas (mensagens, prints, nomes de testemunhas, a cronologia entre a manifestação e a dispensa) e procurar um advogado especialista em direito do trabalho, que vai avaliar se há elementos suficientes e qual o melhor caminho", explicou.

O especialista explica que a proteção vai muito além da opinião política. A Lei 9.029 lista expressamente sexo, origem, raça, cor, estado civil, situação familiar, deficiência, reabilitação profissional e idade. Sobre o posicionamento político, ele alerta para alguns comportamentos que podem ser discriminatórios:

Perguntas sobre voto ou partido na entrevista ou em formulários;

Pesquisa nas redes sociais do candidato com foco em conteúdo político;

Comentários do recrutador sobre "perfil ideológico";

No emprego, mudança de tratamento logo após uma manifestação política, perda de função ou de vantagens;

Ameaça velada de demissão vinculada ao resultado da eleição, ou dispensa sem explicação em período próximo a uma declaração ou postagem.

Fachada do MPT-GO — Foto: Divulgação/MPT-GO

O MPT-GO informou que desde o início do período eleitoral tem lançado publicações nas redes sociais para alertar sobre o que é o assédio eleitoral, informando o que é e o que não é permitido ao empregador ou ao sindicato, e como denunciar.

O trabalhador afetado por esse tipo de conduta no estado de Goiás pode registrar denúncia no MPT-GO, por meio do site oficial, onde é possível solicitar o sigilo da identidade ou realizar a denúncia de forma anônima.

"Não se trata de pensar igual. Trata-se de compartilhar princípios.

A Teoria dos Valores Humanos Básicos, desenvolvida pelo psicólogo Shalom H. Schwartz, demonstra que nossos valores orientam escolhas, comportamentos, prioridades e decisões.

Nas amizades, nas relações profissionais e nas organizações, a compatibilidade de valores favorece a confiança, o pertencimento e a construção de objetivos comuns.

Após os resultados das eleições, muitos empresários têm procurado o Instituto Mara Suassuna para novos processos seletivos, destacando o alinhamento de valores como critério decisivo na contratação.

Mas atenção: alinhamento de valores organizacionais não significa alinhamento político. Significa identificar profissionais que compartilhem princípios como ética, responsabilidade, respeito, integridade e compromisso com os objetivos da empresa.

A diversidade de pensamento fortalece as organizações. O que compromete os resultados não é pensar diferente, mas agir em desacordo com os princípios que sustentam a cultura organizacional.

Sugiro conhecer a teoria de Schwartz. Afinal, nossos valores orientam nossas escolhas, e nossas escolhas revelam quem somos."

articles.title: Como fica o tempo no feriado de Finados? Veja a previsão pelo país | G1
articles.standfirst: Feriado prolongado deve ter pancadas de chuva em grande parte do país, principalmente no Sul, Sudeste e Centro-Oeste. Norte e Nordeste terão calor de até 40°C em algumas áreas.
articles.summary: Feriado prolongado deve ter pancadas de chuva em grande parte do Brasil, principalmente no Sul, Sudeste e Centro-Oeste. Norte e Nordeste podem registrar calor de até 40°C.
articles.body:
Pôr do sol visto da região oeste da capital paulista. — Foto: Aloisio Mauricio/Fotoarena/Estadão Conteúdo

O feriado prolongado de Finados , celebrado na próxima segunda-feira (2 de novembro), deve ser marcado por períodos de sol, calor e pancadas de chuva em grande parte do Brasil.

Entre sábado (31) e segunda-feira (2), a previsão é de que temporais atinjam áreas do Sul, Sudeste e Centro-Oeste.

A chuva deve ganhar força com o deslocamento de áreas de baixa pressão e a presença de umidade na atmosfera , condições que favorecem a formação de nuvens carregadas e podem provocar temporais em diferentes regiões do país.

Segundo a Climatempo, não há previsão de passagem de uma nova frente fria pelo país durante o feriado prolongado, mas a combinação entre calor, umidade e circulação dos ventos deve manter as condições para chuva em quase todas as regiões .

As maiores temperaturas devem se concentrar no Norte e no Nordeste, onde os termômetros podem se aproximar dos 40°C em algumas localidades.

🌦️ Veja os principais destaques para o feriado por região do país:

Sul: o sábado (31) deve ter períodos de sol e pancadas isoladas, principalmente no Paraná e em Santa Catarina. No domingo (1º), a chuva pode ganhar força à tarde e à noite. Já na segunda-feira (2), há previsão de pancadas fortes nos dois estados;

Sudeste: há previsão de chuva nos três dias. No sábado (31), as pancadas podem ocorrer a qualquer hora. No domingo (1º) e na segunda-feira (2), o sol deve aparecer pela manhã, mas há risco de temporais à tarde e à noite;

Centro-Oeste: sábado (31) e domingo (1º) terão períodos de sol e calor, seguidos por pancadas de chuva, principalmente à tarde. Na segunda-feira (2), a chuva pode começar pela manhã em Mato Grosso do Sul;

Nordeste: predomínio de sol e calor durante todo o feriadão, com temperaturas de até 40°C no interior. A chuva deve ficar mais concentrada em áreas do Maranhão, Piauí e Bahia;

Norte: pancadas de chuva podem ocorrer a qualquer hora entre sábado (31) e segunda-feira (2) no Amazonas, Acre e Rondônia. Em Roraima, no Amapá e no extremo norte do Pará, o tempo deve ficar mais seco.

No Sul, a previsão é de um fim de semana de temperaturas mais elevadas durante as tardes, mas as madrugadas ainda devem ser relativamente frias nas áreas serranas.

Ainda de acordo com a Climatempo, os termômetros podem ficar próximos dos 10°C nas áreas mais altas das serras gaúcha e catarinense e em alguns municípios próximos à fronteira do Rio Grande do Sul com o Uruguai.

No sábado, o sol deve aparecer por mais tempo em boa parte do território gaúcho. As pancadas de chuva ficam mais concentradas no norte e no leste do estado, incluindo a Região Metropolitana de Porto Alegre e as áreas serranas.

No Paraná e em Santa Catarina, a previsão também indica períodos de sol no sábado, mas a chuva pode atingir principalmente o leste e o norte paranaense e o leste e o sul catarinense.

Já no domingo (1º), a possibilidade de chuva aumenta nos dois estados, especialmente durante a tarde e a noite, quando podem ocorrer pancadas acompanhadas por raios.

Na segunda-feira (2), dia de Finados , a chuva pode começar pela manhã no centro-oeste do Paraná e de Santa Catarina e atingir outras áreas desses estados ao longo da tarde. Há possibilidade de pancadas fortes em alguns pontos.

Em Curitiba (PR), os termômetros devem variar entre 15°C e 25°C no feriado. Florianópolis (SC) pode registrar mínima de 21°C e máxima de 24°C. Em Porto Alegre (RS), a previsão indica temperaturas entre 18°C e 27°C.

No Sudeste, a chuva deve atingir áreas dos quatro estados durante o fim de semana prolongado.

Uma área de baixa pressão atmosférica próxima à costa deve favorecer a formação de nuvens carregadas no sábado, deixando o céu mais encoberto em São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro, Minas Gerais e Espírito Santo.

As pancadas podem ocorrer em diferentes momentos do dia, mas devem ganhar intensidade principalmente durante a tarde e a noite.

No domingo e na segunda-feira, o afastamento desse sistema deve permitir períodos maiores de sol pela manhã. Ainda assim, a combinação de calor e umidade mantém a possibilidade de pancadas acompanhadas por raios no restante do dia.

🌧️ Há previsão de chuva forte nos três dias do feriado prolongado em diferentes áreas do Sudeste. Nas praias, o sol pode aparecer por períodos maiores no domingo e na segunda-feira, mas a possibilidade de chuva continua alta, principalmente à tarde.

Na cidade de São Paulo (SP), as temperaturas devem ficar próximas dos 25°C no feriado, e há previsão de pancadas durante a tarde e a noite.

No Rio de Janeiro (RJ), a segunda-feira pode ter mínima de 21°C e máxima de 29°C. Em Belo Horizonte (MG), os termômetros devem variar entre 20°C e 26°C, também sob previsão de chuva.

Mapa mostra previsão de chuva para esta quinta (29/10) em todo o Brasil. — Foto: CPTEC/Inpe

No Centro-Oeste, o calor e a grande quantidade de umidade devem favorecer pancadas de chuva ao longo dos três dias.

Mato Grosso, Goiás e o Distrito Federal podem ter várias horas de sol, principalmente durante as manhãs. Ao longo da tarde, porém, a formação de nuvens carregadas deve provocar pancadas que podem ser fortes e acompanhadas por raios e rajadas de vento.

A previsão indica temperaturas entre 35°C e 39°C em áreas de Mato Grosso e do norte de Goiás. No Distrito Federal, as máximas devem variar entre 28°C e 30°C.

Em Mato Grosso do Sul, a chuva deve ocorrer principalmente durante as tardes de sábado e domingo. Na segunda-feira, as pancadas podem começar mais cedo, inclusive em Campo Grande (MS), e atingir grande parte do estado.

No Nordeste, o feriado prolongado deve ter predomínio de sol e calor em grande parte dos estados .

Segundo a Climatempo, a possibilidade de chuva será menor do que nas demais regiões, principalmente nas capitais e nas áreas litorâneas.

As exceções ficam no interior do Maranhão e do Piauí e no oeste e sudoeste da Bahia, onde podem ocorrer pancadas localizadas durante o fim de semana.

Temperaturas mínimas previstas para esta quinta (29/10) em todo o Brasil. — Foto: CPTEC/Inpe

As temperaturas podem variar entre 37°C e 40°C em áreas do sertão, do interior do Maranhão e do Piauí e do oeste baiano.

Nas capitais, o calor também deve continuar. Fortaleza (CE) pode chegar aos 31°C na segunda-feira, enquanto João Pessoa (PB) e Recife (PE) devem registrar máximas próximas dos 29°C.

Já no Norte, a previsão indica maior frequência de chuva no Amazonas, Acre e Rondônia, inclusive durante as manhãs.

Nesses estados, as pancadas podem ocorrer a qualquer momento, com possibilidade de chuva moderada a forte em algumas localidades.

No Tocantins e em grande parte do Pará, o sol deve aparecer durante várias horas, mas ainda podem ocorrer pancadas isoladas durante as tardes e noites.

Em Roraima, no Amapá e no extremo norte do Pará, a tendência é de tempo mais firme, com pouca possibilidade de chuva.

As temperaturas devem continuar elevadas nessas áreas, podendo chegar perto dos 40°C em alguns municípios.

Em Porto Velho (RO), a máxima prevista para o feriado é de 33°C, com possibilidade de pancadas à tarde. Rio Branco (AC) pode registrar até 34°C, enquanto Manaus (AM) deve ter máxima próxima dos 31°C.

articles.title: Europe's youth are protesting - and feeling locked out of a future
articles.summary: The last month has seen youth-driven demonstrations across Europe. What connects them?
articles.body:
From Milan, to Marseille, to Madrid and in so many other cities across Europe, streets have erupted in colourful, passionate protests in recent weeks. While most started peacefully, a large number ended in shocking scenes of violence and looting. There have been allegations of radical left-wing groups sparking riots intentionally and reports of police heavy-handedness.

We've seen thousands rallying in Rome and Florence. Hundreds of thousands across France. In Madrid, an encampment of tents has occupied a city-centre square since late September. In Lisbon, tens of thousands of mostly young people marched earlier this month. Tear gas and water cannon were used on protesters in Brussels, after young men dressed in black, their faces covered to hide their identities, threw rocks and firecrackers at police. In Albania, demonstrators alleging government corruption are demanding that their Prime Minister Edi Rama – already 13 years in power – stand down.

This continent feels volatile, socially and politically.

I've spent years in Europe reporting from a multitude of demonstrations, both peaceful and violent. I remember well the ardent Catalan pro-independence marches of 2017, the desperation and Molotov cocktails flying through Athens' streets during the 2015 Greek debt crisis, and various outbreaks of violence in France during President Emmanuel Macron's first term in office, sparked by fuel tax and pension reform proposals.

But this feels different. Protests are exploding simultaneously across Europe and the majority of demonstrators – both peaceful and violent – are young. Some really young. Among those arrested, there's an eyebrow-raising number of minors. Over half of those detained in Barcelona scuffles last weekend were under 18. Minors were among those apprehended by police in Milan after clashes, according to Italy's LaPresse news agency.

Europe's governments, for the most part, have been careful to distinguish between looters and rioters on the one hand, and loud but peaceful, legally organised demonstrations on the other. The latter tend to focus around a particular cause. In the current protest wave, placards and chants mainly take aim at education grievances, social inequalities and the rising cost of living – though each country also comes with its own unique set of complaints.

What has triggered this public fury in Europe's youth, seemingly so quickly? Are all these demonstrations in some way interwoven? And with major European elections on the horizon, how will governments choose to respond – listening to protesters' concerns, or playing the law and order card to win support from older voters?

Students have taken to the streets in France, Belgium, Ireland, Spain, Portugal, Italy, Greece, Serbia and Albania – a more than 1,000-mile span of the continent.

Demonstrations are often organised in an ad hoc way via TikTok or Instagram. Belgium's interior minister has complained about what he calls the "TikTokisation" of protests.

Student unions play a role in organising marches, but they are also inspired by the actions of peers in other countries, even other continents. Think of the so-called Cockroach student movement in India – a Gen Z social and political protest movement that emerged in May this year, starting with criticism of the Indian education system.

France, where the current wave of student protests kicked off in late September, fuelled by student complaints over staff shortages and dilapidated buildings, is a stand-out catalyst in Europe. There's a saying in neighbouring Belgium: whenever it pours in Paris, it at least drizzles in Brussels. The Belgian capital and the town of Liège have also now seen weeks of protesting youngsters.

In Barcelona this weekend, students were encouraged to demonstrate under the social media hashtag #InstitutsIndignats, echoing the French slogan, Lycées Indignés (Outraged High Schools).

In Athens, 17-year-old Greek school pupil Yiannis Papanikolaou told AFP: "School buildings are terrible and poorly maintained… I think something might change, because of what France is doing, France will spur Greece."

There's a continent-wide sense of economic malaise felt by large numbers of young people – and it goes far beyond education. They worry about the environment, and fret that AI will rob them of job opportunities. They fear the spiralling cost of living could prevent them from finishing their education and stop them buying or renting a home big enough to start a family.

In Madrid and in Lisbon, frustration has focused on the prohibitive price tag attached to housing. Portuguese Instagram-linked campaigns stated "enough is enough" and called on people to take to the streets as peers had done in Spain.

In Lisbon, Carolina ⁠Cruz, 26, a PhD student and biology researcher, said she faces losing her home as her rental contract nears expiry. "I'm the first person in my family to enter a doctoral programme and even with all the studying I've done, I still can't make it," she told Reuters.

It's an anger shared by 22-year-old Riccardo, a protester in Italy's financial capital, Milan. "Even if we don't manage to throw the country into chaos like in France or block every road like in Spain, the aim is at least people will start talking about these issues again," he told AFP.

And it's certainly not just young people on the left of politics who are angry. At the presidential campaign launch of French nationalist Marine Le Pen last weekend, young supporters described different concerns to me. Calling themselves the "silent majority" – not (yet) out demonstrating – they say they also worry deeply about "uncontrolled immigration" and safety on France's streets, as well as the cost of living.

The outpouring of discontent has spread beyond young people to include trade unions, France's disparate Yellow Jacket movement that protested against the cost of living crisis during Macron's first term, and other citizens' initiatives. This weekend, Kent in coastal southern England saw two protests, one for and one against immigration.

This miscellaneous mix of protests can seem confusing.

Mark Leonard, the director of the European Council of Foreign Relations, speaks of a build-up of cascading, competing crises in Europe, none of which have ever been properly resolved, he says. That sense of pent-up anger is now bubbling over onto the streets.

"One crisis layers on top of the other," he told me. "The financial crisis of 2007-8, the migrant crisis of 2015, the environmental crisis, Covid, inflation after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022 and now again with the war in the Gulf."

Leonard says different "tribes" have emerged out of these crises. Social media consumption and algorithms harden their differing perspectives, leading to a real sense of polarisation in Europe.

"We've already seen this in the US," says Leonard. "A sense of 'my crisis is more important than your crisis'."

Nathalie Tocci, a former Italian government adviser who is now a politics professor at Johns Hopkins University, tells me we shouldn't be so taken aback by the protests, or the youth engagement in them.

"We tend to think of youngsters as politically switched off and disinterested. We think they don't bother to go out to vote etc, but they are truly engaged," she told me, "just in a different, more grassroots way. Think of the "Fridays for the Future [environmental movement] across Europe a few years ago, or the demonstrations against Israel's actions in Gaza after 7 October.

She points to the student-led protest movement in Serbia, which recently defeated long-standing leader Aleksandar Vučić in parliamentary elections. "It's quite something. They kept going and going, for more than two years. What sticking power will these new European street demos have? That's not yet clear."

And what about the looting and the violence?

Intelligence services in France and Belgium have described looting on the edges of legally approved protests as mainly opportunistic.

The rioting, they suggest, is a mixture of "mindless violence" – also identified by the Spanish authorities in Barcelona to describe clashes there at the weekend - plus mayhem intentionally orchestrated by youth from ultra-left radical groups.

Tocci reminded me that, in Italy, you can hear the word "maranza" being used by some Italians upset by the perpetrators of destruction seemingly for the sake of it: smashing or burning cars or public bins, for example.

In France, rioters are often described as "casseurs" – people who break things. But in private, some use a more politically charged term – "racaille". Like "maranza" in Italy, it's pejorative slang, generally used to describe disaffected, rowdy urban youths frequently from working-class and/or immigrant backgrounds. It was used in October 2005 by then-French Interior Minister Nicolas Sarkozy, to describe young delinquents and rioters during a tense visit to the housing projects of Paris suburb Argenteuil.

French media has also asked whether there's been an alliance of convenience, however informal or incidental, between two groups of youths: ultra-left activists and young people from France's disadvantaged neighbourhoods. Like the anti-capitalist left, youth from public housing projects on the outskirts of French cities (known as the banlieues) often feel discriminated against, and complain of police heavy handedness towards them.

The political right and centre in France, including Macron, blame left-wing radical groups and "delinquents" for planning the riots. In contrast to Le Pen's National Rally Party, they have not mentioned a link with past or current immigration to France.

Critics accuse anti-immigration parties in Europe of trying to capitalise from the riots to score political points. In Belgium, the anti-immigration opposition Flemish nationalist party, Vlaams Belang, appeared to blame migrants for violence in Liège and Brussels, describing the riots as "imported" and blaming a failure of integration and of open borders. Belgium's Interior Minister Bernard Quentin has pointed the finger at ultra-left groups.

Fresh mass demonstrations have been planned over the next days in France and in Italy.

Governments are trying to crack down on the violence. There have been thousands of arrests, and Italy and France have promised to impose a "you break it, you pay for it" policy for rioters.

Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni is also making parents of minors liable for damage caused by their kids, including deducting welfare support received by the family. The Civil Code in France already holds parents who live with their children liable for damage they cause.

But some of these European governments may not be in power for long. All the big EU countries have been holding, or will hold, key elections in the coming months. France's presidential vote is considered the most pivotal for Europe. Le Pen is consistently polling far ahead of her rivals. It's assumed the unrest on French streets is helping her, thanks to her party's law and order message.

In Spain, Italy, Germany and Poland, nationalist, tough-on-immigration parties are also polling well. These parties promise to restore order and national pride. Leonard believes populist or non-traditional parties on the left and the right have become "crisis entrepreneurs", using the turbulent situation in Europe to attract disaffected voters.

Meanwhile, Europe's political mainstream faces a crisis of leadership, says Grégoire Roos, director of Europe at the Chatham House think tank.

I would argue they also face a crisis of legitimacy. The fact that so many people - the young and not so young - are out protesting indicates they have failed to get on top of things.

Europe's car makers are in crisis. Will the threat of war rescue them?

Spain and China are cosying up - to the anger of many in the EU

How population decline is exposing Germany's old divides

But it's not at all clear that new elections will resolve public frustration. France is so polarised, for example, that if Le Pen were to become president, many predict her opponents would fill French streets in anger.

Modern Europe is built on an assumption that citizens pay taxes and obey laws. In exchange, they get good public services, like education and healthcare, personal safety and a stable society that follows certain rules and regulations.

But this "social contract" has clearly eroded, says Roos.

Looking at the ferment on Europe's streets, this moment of protest looks likely to continue.

articles.title: In 2022, four friends sold homemade cinnamon rolls through messages and local deliveries in Utah, four years later Sunshine Buns has raised $7 million and expanded onto Target shelves nationwide
articles.summary: A Utah frozen cinnamon roll company that began as a home-baking project among four friends has raised $7 million (£5.5 million) in Series A funding.
articles.body: A Utah frozen cinnamon roll company that began as a home-baking project among four friends has raised $7 million (£5.5 million) in Series A funding. The money will help it grow its reach in stores across the country. Sunshine Buns, based in Orem, announced the new investment as its products arrive in the freezer aisles of Target stores nationwide and in Southern California Costco warehouses. The funding round will pay for more production capacity, more product on hand, more marketing, and more hiring, according to industry trade outlet Food Business News. The business was founded in 2022 by Chrisi Hammer, her husband Matt, and their friends Brian and Kass Martin. The brand is built on a family cinnamon roll recipe created more than 45 years ago by Chrisi Hammer’s mother, who is lovingly known as Mema. “Mema had her first cinnamon roll in the 1970s and knew she could make something better,” Chrisi Hammer explained in an interview published by the Startup State Initiative, a Utah state government business platform. “She worked for years to create the perfect recipe, and boy, did she deliver.”From theatre chat to immediate sell-outThe four co-founders had talked for a long time about starting a business together. The choice to turn the family recipe into a company came during an evening out. “One night, as the four of us were attending a show at the Hale Theater in Orem, we realized we needed to launch the business,” Chrisi Hammer told the Startup State Initiative. “We started an Instagram page and officially accepted orders the very next day, then sold out in a matter of minutes. That was when we knew we were onto something.” At first, the team ran a home-based delivery service. They took orders through private social media messages and hand-delivered fresh trays of cinnamon rolls to local customers. Strong demand led the founders to open their first physical shop in Orem. They then moved into making frozen food for wholesale. The brand’s frozen rolls have real cream cheese frosting and 8 grams of protein per bun. They come in three flavors: original, cookies and cream, and strawberries and cream.Supermarket expansion and Series A backingThe brand first entered freezer aisles through regional grocers such as Hy-Vee, Gelson’s, and Bristol Farms. It then moved up to major national chains, including Target and Costco. Food Business News reported that the new $7 million Series A money will directly pay for the inventory needed to supply these large retail networks. “We have big plans for our buns, and our goal is to build Sunshine Buns into something special people can find wherever they shop,” Kass Martin, co-founder of Sunshine Buns, said in a statement carried by Food Business News. “We’re excited to keep growing and bring some much-needed fun to freezer aisles across the country.” The company’s fast rise from a neighborhood delivery business to a national retail brand drew wider attention at the 2025 Silicon Slopes Summit. There, Sunshine Buns won top honors in the Startup Alley small business competition.Local business support and community growthLooking back on the company’s journey, the founders credited much of their success to local mentors and Utah’s startup network. They pointed to guidance from established regional brands, including Gimme Beauty, Retail Collective, and Mixhers. “We have been very fortunate to have many mentors through our journey this far,” Chrisi Hammer stated in her interview with the Startup State Initiative. “The Utah startup ecosystem has also been vital to our success. The community truly rallies behind its own. It’s encouraging to grow a business where the people believe in and support each other.” Chrisi Hammer also gave advice to people hoping to turn a side project into a full-time business. She urged them not to wait to take the first step. “Just start,” Chrisi Hammer advised via the Startup State Initiative. “It’s going to be hard, amazing, taxing, and glorious all at the same time. You’ll never have everything figured out, but the truth is, it’s always a good time to start.” With the Series A funding secured, Sunshine Buns plans to start more product development projects. It also plans to widen its reach across regional and national supermarket chains.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Conservative James O'Keefe charged with unlawful voting in election stunt
articles.summary: Prosecutors alleged the pair misrepresented their identities by giving election judges the names of other people.
articles.body:
Two conservative activists who filmed a stunt undercover at a Minnesota polling site have been charged with unlawful voting and identity theft, prosecutors said.

James Edward O'Keefe and Cam Higby are accused of trying to sow doubt in the state's voting systems after sharing a video that shows them in Islamic attire and using fake accents while interacting with poll workers.

Prosecutors allege the pair misrepresented their identities by giving election judges the names of registered voters in the precinct without those voters' knowledge or permission.

Higby told the BBC he sought to "expose vulnerabilities" in the voting system and alleged the state is now trying to take away his right to vote.

"This investigation was conducted to expose vulnerabilities in the Minnesota voting system, which affects all Americans," Higby, a 26-year-old political commentator, said.

"I never voted, I never signed an affidavit, and I never violated a law," he continued. "For showing how Minnesota abuses votes, they seek to take mine away from me permanently."

The Hennepin County Attorney's Office confirmed neither of the men signed the required oath to confirm their address. But the prosecutors said both men "intentionally" misrepresented their identities when applying for ballots.

Unlawful voting and identity theft are felony charges.

In the recorded incident from August, the provocateurs were attempting to highlight a Minnesota law that allows registered voters to vouch for the identity and address of up to eight people.

The law is intended to assist people who recently moved to the state to vote - not to impersonate other registered voters.

At the time, Higby captioned the video: "I dressed as a Muslim woman and Minneapolis poll workers were prepared to allow me and an army of other foreigners to fraudulently vote without verifying who any of us are."

State law holds that no individual can intentionally misrepresent their identity in applying for a ballot, depositing a ballot in a ballot box or attempting to vote by means of a voting machine or electronic voting system.

Minnesota Secretary of State Steve Simon, the state's chief election officer, said in a statement on Wednesday that "any attempt to disrupt or deceive our election workers will not be tolerated".

He added, "Polling places are the heart of our democracy and should be places of safety and peace."

It was not immediately clear when O'Keefe and Higby are due in court.

The BBC has contacted O'Keefe for comment.

O'Keefe, 42, is the founder of Project Veritas, a right-wing activist group and media company that seeks to investigate and expose corruption. The group is known to produce secretly recorded encounters. After being ousted from Project Veritas, he founded O'Keefe Media Group.

articles.title: Manhunt grows for escaped murderer who may have left area where truck was ditched
articles.summary: Jacob Morley, who fatally shot a co-worker, escaped Sunday from a prison in Tennessee. The work truck he allegedly stole was found in Illinois.
articles.body: Jacob Morley, a convicted killer on the loose since Sunday, has no known connection to the small Illinois town where the truck he is accused of stealing was found, the police chief said Wednesday. “What we have seen kind of leads us in the direction that he’s not still here. But that doesn’t mean that we’ve stopped looking,” Marion Police Chief David Fitts said. Morley, 28, convicted of killing a co-worker in 2022, was serving a life sentence when he escaped from Northwest Correctional Complex in Tiptonville, Tennessee, sometime before 11:30 p.m. Sunday, officials there said. Morley had stolen a work truck, and early Tuesday that truck was found behind a business in Marion, a town of around 16,000 that is around 100 miles north of Tiptonville, authorities in Marion and Tennessee said. There have been no reports in Marion of any other stolen vehicles, and there was no evidence around the truck that was found, Fitts said. There have also been no confirmed sightings, he said. “There’s really nowhere for him to go here where he wouldn’t be recognized. His face is all over the news,” Fitts said. Morley has no known connection to Marion or southern Illinois, he said. “Have no idea why he would come here, other than I-57 is a major interstate and it runs right through the middle of our town,” Fitts said. “And I don’t know, maybe he was low on gas and just pulled off. I don’t know.” Morley was convicted of first-degree murder, abuse of a corpse, tampering with evidence and aggravated burglary after a trial in February 2025. He also pleaded guilty to theft of property. He was accused of shooting Cody Birchfield in the back of the head in 2022, according to court documents. Birchfield’s body was found in a large metal box under Morley’s residence, the documents say. Birchfield’s sister, Carrie Norman, said Wednesday that “it feels like a scary movie.” The family, she said, “have to go back through the experience — once again. Once again, because you don’t know where he’s at, but you know what he’s capable of.” Also Wednesday, the reward for information leading to Morley’s arrest increased from $2,500 to $15,000, a combined sum from the Tennessee governor’s office, the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation and the U.S. Marshals Service, the bureau said. Fitts said he wished Morley had been caught, but he urged people not to take things into their own hands. “This is really frustrating that we can’t find him. Somebody will eventually, I have no doubt in my mind. I wish it was us so we could catch him now,” Fitts said. “But, and I just want to let our people know that, again, don’t approach him. Call 911. We’ll handle it.” Around 11:30 p.m. Sunday, prison staff members confirmed that Morley was unaccounted for and conducted an emergency count and search of the facility, the Tennessee Department of Correction said. Security video showed Morley “breached the perimeter fence and exited the facility in his TDOC uniform,” the department said. The department has not given more details about how the escape occurred, which it said Wednesday is under investigation.

articles.title: 'Ballot' jolt for Congress: BJP-JD(S) sweeps all 4 Karnataka MLC seats
articles.summary: BENGALURU: The BJP-JD(S) NDA swept all four Karnataka Legislative Council seats in polls held through ballot papers, dealing a blow to governing Congress
articles.body: BENGALURU: The BJP-JD(S) NDA swept all four Karnataka Legislative Council seats in polls held through ballot papers, dealing a blow to governing Congress ahead of the 2028 assembly polls.DK Shivakumar, facing his first polls since taking over as chief minister, said Congress would take corrective measures in view of these results. "We respect the verdict. We had expected to win two seats, but that did not happen. The Bengaluru Teachers' result, particularly, was unexpected. We will review it. Although we lost, we secured a good number of votes," Shivakumar said.Opposition BJP mocked Shivakumar after the outcome as Congress has been demanding a switch from EVMs to ballot papers. "DK, it's done, bro! NDA sweeps all four Teachers' and Graduates' constituencies in the MLC elections," the party posted on X."MLC elections in 28 seats across 4 big states -- Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Bihar and Karnataka. Elections held using ballot papers. Guess how many seats Congress won?" PM Modi said on X. It was an apparent taunt at Congress's continuing troubles and a rebuke to the opposition party's claim that BJP's successes are because of the EVMs and electoral rolls.19 ministers on poll job, Cong gets 0 The polls covered 19 districts, comprising nearly two-thirds of the state, including the home districts of former CM Siddaramaiah and AICC president Mallikarjun Kharge. JD(S) candidate AP Ranganath wrested Bengaluru Teachers' seat from Congress, defeating sitting MLC Puttanna by 908 votes, while BJP won the other three seats.In North East Teachers' seat, Shashil G Namoshi beat Sharanappa Mattur by 3,297 votes. In West Graduates' constituency, SV Sankanur posted a hat-trick of wins, beating Congress's Mohan Limbikai by 9,323, while in South East Graduates' seat, KM Suresh trounced Shashi Hulikuntemath by 23,098 votes.KPCC president BK Hariprasad, who was also facing his first test at the hustings since his appointment, said the party will conduct a comprehensive review of its organisational and political shortcomings.Multiple factors are said to have dealt a blow to Congress. According to party insiders, Shivakumar, despite himself being a master poll strategist, had assigned 19 ministers to oversee 133 assembly segments under the four constituencies that went to the polls, while he himself was busy with protests over SIR, Dasara preparations and his political trips to Delhi.The failure of ministers to deliver the goods is being seen by some political functionaries as a reflection of growing differences within the party since Shivakumar became CM. Teachers' resentment over govt's failure to restore the old pension scheme may have cost Congress both the teachers' seats.On the other hand, BJP and JD(S) showed better coordination this time around than in previous polls. articles.title: Dem strategist shrugs off Alaska ballot scandal on MS NOW, insists 'this stuff happens all the time'
articles.summary: Democratic strategist Adrienne Elrod dismissed the Alaska ballot scandal, comparing it to Republican donors propping up RFK Jr. against Joe Biden in 2024.
articles.body: Democratic strategist Adrienne Elrod chalked up Wednesday's revelations about an alleged Democratic scheme to influence Alaska's Senate race as something that "happens all the time," comparing it to Republican support for Robert F. Kennedy Jr.'s 2024 presidential bid against then-President Joe Biden during the 2024 election cycle. The New York Times published a bombshell report alleging that Democratic operatives recruited a man named Dan Sullivan to run as a spoiler candidate against incumbent Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan of Alaska, potentially aiding his Democratic opponent, former Rep. Mary Peltola. Appearing on an MS NOW panel, Elrod was quick to shrug off the controversy. PELTOLA CAMPAIGN'S ALLEGED DAN SULLIVAN SPOILER PLOT TAKES NEW TURN AS DOJ FACES MAJOR LEGAL HURDLE "Some of this stuff happens all the time," Elrod reacted. "Let's not forget that ... RFK Jr., when he ran against Joe Biden, Republicans propped him up, a lot of Trump donors were giving him money because they thought he would dig into some of Biden's supporters. And then he ran as an independent. They thought he would draw away supporters from Biden. It actually had the opposite effect. "The bottom line is this stuff happens all the time. There are tactics that both campaigns can use. ... It is very clear, as you mentioned, who is the incumbent. So, if you're a Republican or any voter in Alaska, and you want to support the incumbent, you know who you're voting for," Elrod added noting she hadn't read the Times report. MS NOW anchor Peter Alexander said the "funny business" involving Democrats in Alaska was "not illegal" and pointed out that the Republican senator is listed as "incumbent" on the ballot, which he argued undermined the Trump administration's concerns about voter confusion. SCHIFF ACCUSES DOJ OF TRYING TO 'SUBVERT' ELECTIONS AS GOP ALLEGES SAME-NAME CANDIDATE MEANT TO CONFUSE VOTERS Republicans have long been suspicious about the candidacy of Daniel J. Sullivan Jr., a retired teacher who is among four Senate candidates listed on Alaska's rank-choice ballot. The Department of Justice filed a lawsuit against the state of Alaska seeking to block certification of the election results if the incumbent senator loses and votes cast for the other Sullivan could have changed the outcome. "In the summer of 2025, a staffer for Mary Peltola, the Alaska Democrat who was eyeing a run for Senate, received unusual instructions from top campaign aides: Find as many people named Dan Sullivan in Alaska as you can," the Times began its report Wednesday. "The staffer complied, combing through voter records to produce a list of Dan Sullivans from across the state. ... [I]f the Peltola campaign or its allies could track down and persuade another Dan Sullivan to run for Senate, the confusion could cost the senator crucial votes on the state’s unusual, four-person ballot. The plan worked." CLICK HERE FOR THE LATEST MEDIA AND CULTURE NEWS According to Peltola's former campaign manager, Elisa Rios, Peltola was not directly involved in the scheme but was "definitely aware." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "The Peltola campaign has repeatedly denied any involvement in his candidacy," the Times wrote. "But The Times has found, based on interviews and text messages, along with documents prepared for a potential lawsuit against the campaign, that not only did Ms. Peltola’s team work with people trying to recruit Mr. Sullivan to run for Senate, but the effort was much broader. The group worked to coax other would-be spoilers into the race, to dilute the incumbent’s support and help catapult the Democrat to victory."

articles.title: A barber who carved a wooden elephant for his wife in the 1920s went on to create a remarkable collection of sculptures now preserved in a museum
articles.summary: In the late 1920s, Elijah Pierce made a small wooden elephant for his wife, a modest gift that gave him a reason to keep carving.
articles.body: In the late 1920s, Elijah Pierce made a small wooden elephant for his wife, a modest gift that gave him a reason to keep carving. He worked as a barber in Columbus, Ohio, and fitted the hobby around the demands of his shop. What began with a single animal gradually expanded into a much larger body of work, including carved figures drawn from his religious beliefs and memories of childhood. Pierce had been interested in carving since he was young, long before he settled into barbering. Decades later, his sculptures became part of a collection held by the Columbus Museum, where more than 100 examples of his work documented an artistic practice that had developed over a lifetime.Elijah Pierce’s childhood on a Southern farm sparked an early interest in carvingPierce grew up in the rural South, where his father expected him to work on the family farm alongside his brothers. The work did not appeal to him in the same way it did to the other boys. He preferred to spend time outdoors, using the trees around his home as places to cut names, animals and small figures into the bark. The activity gave him an early opportunity to make things with his hands, even though it was far removed from the work his family expected him to do.Pierce later described himself as an unusual child because of his reluctance to follow the same path as his brothers. His interest in carving was already apparent, but it was not yet a settled occupation. As a teenager, he left home and travelled across the country, riding freight trains and moving between places before eventually making his way to Columbus. There, he established a barber shop and built a working life that would provide him with the time and space to continue carving.How a wooden elephant inspired Elijah Pierce to build a carved animal collectionThe small elephant Pierce carved for his wife in the late 1920s marked a turning point in his work. She liked the gift, encouraging him to make more. He began thinking about creating a whole collection of animals, rather than treating each carving as an isolated piece. The idea developed into what he imagined as a wooden zoo.His barber shop became the setting for much of this activity. Between appointments and during quieter moments, he worked on his sculptures while continuing to earn his living cutting hair. Barbering remained his profession, but carving occupied the spare hours that might otherwise have been left unused. The two activities continued side by side for years, with the shop serving both its everyday purpose and, in a sense, as a place where his collection took shape.Pierce had been carving since childhood, yet his wife's encouragement gave him a more defined project to pursue. From there, the range of subjects he worked on grew beyond animals.Elijah Pierce saw his carving talent as a gift from GodPierce's work increasingly reflected the religious experiences of his upbringing. Biblical stories and figures became recurring subjects, alongside the animals that had first inspired his carving. His sculptures drew on scenes and teachings he had encountered as a child, translating familiar religious narratives into forms he could shape from wood.He regarded his ability as a gift from God. For Pierce, carving was connected to the religious message he wanted to communicate, even though he had not delivered every sermon he might have imagined preaching. He described his purpose in terms of making the sermons he had never preached, a phrase that linked his creative work to his faith.From a barber shop to a museum collectionPierce continued to carve while working as a barber in Columbus, developing a body of work that encompassed animals, human figures and religious scenes. His route into sculpture had not followed formal artistic training. It began with a childhood habit, continued through years of working life and gained fresh direction after he made a gift for his wife.The Columbus Museum eventually held more than 100 of his carvings, preserving a substantial selection of objects produced through this long-running practice. The collection brought together works associated with different aspects of Pierce's interests, from the animals that followed the elephant to figures inspired by biblical narratives. Seen together, they offered a record of how his carving developed beyond its original purpose as a personal pastime.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: ‘Our democracy is in danger’: Judge blocks Trump administration’s California ballot push
articles.summary: A federal judge has rejected the Trump administration’s request to set aside up to 20,000 mail-in ballots in California over allegations that the voters
articles.body: A federal judge has rejected the Trump administration’s request to set aside up to 20,000 mail-in ballots in California over allegations that the voters may be non-citizens, warning that the move would “wreak havoc and disrupt the election that is already underway”.US District Judge David O Carter issued the ruling on Wednesday, rejecting the Justice Department’s demand that California delay counting the ballots until the citizenship status of the voters could be verified. The decision came as more than 3.7 million people had already voted in the state, according to court proceedings cited in Associated Press (AP) reports.“Eroded trust in our democracy is irreparable. Once a vote is segregated, lasting harm has occurred,” Carter wrote in his order.“If the Executive can discount votes and threaten an ongoing election due to unproven allegations, then our democracy is in danger. This Court declines to be a party to such process,” he added.Why did the court reject the request?The Republican administration sued California election officials in mid-October, alleging that they had failed to meet a 48-hour deadline to review a list of 20,000 people whom federal authorities suspected of being non-citizens on the voter rolls.According to CNN, the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) had claimed in July that 190,000 registered California voters could be ineligible because they were foreign nationals. The government subsequently provided election officials with a list of 20,000 purported “high confidence” matches on a password-protected thumb drive and gave the state 48 hours to act.However, local election officials found during their initial review that many names were either absent from voter rolls or listed as suspended, meaning those individuals would not receive mail-in ballots. Officials also found indications that some people identified as likely non-citizens were born in the United States, CNN reported. DHS officials disputed aspects of this assessment in court declarations.Carter said segregating ballots at this stage would force counties to develop new procedures and risk disenfranchising voters. He also held that the request could violate the National Voter Registration Act, which restricts certain changes to voter registration within 90 days of an election.California mails ballots to all 23 million registered voters. Court filings show more than 500,000 ballots had already been processed, with envelopes verified and ballots removed, making it virtually impossible to trace individual ballots, Los Angeles County officials testified.The US justice department said it would immediately appeal the ruling. First Assistant US Attorney Bill Essayli defended the administration’s position in a social media post.“Every day, more ballots are processed by election officials,” Essayli wrote. “This ongoing emergency disenfranchises American citizens through dilution.”He had previously argued that segregating ballots would preserve the status quo rather than prevent votes from being counted later.The legal dispute comes amid wider federal efforts to scrutinise voter eligibility ahead of the midterm elections, including similar litigation in Washington state.You use AI every day. articles.title: Hello Kitty maker cuts ties with Japanese spy drama after China backlash
articles.summary: Sanrio has apologised after its merchandise line with Japanese TV series Vivant drew criticism.
articles.body:
Sanrio, the company behind Hello Kitty, has apologised and ended its merchandise partnership with a controversial Japanese TV show after drawing backlash in China.

Vivant, a popular spy thriller, has been widely slammed in Chinese state media and by Chinese social media users for its depiction of Chinese agents using brutal torture tactics on a Japanese operative.

The criticism has extended to the internationally beloved Hello Kitty and her friends, including My Melody and Cinnamoroll, who were featured in merchandise dressed as characters from the show.

Sanrio said it terminated its collaboration with Vivant after determining that it "contained elements inconsistent with Sanrio's core values".

"Since its inception, Sanrio has consistently used its characters to convey values such as care and connection, and remains committed to its corporate philosophy of fostering harmony among all people," Sanrio said in the statement late on Wednesday.

"We take the feedback we have received regarding this incident very seriously. Moving forward, we will strengthen our review processes for all future collaborative projects."

China-Japan ties have plunged to their lowest point in years, since Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's comments on Taiwan last November sparked a diplomatic firestorm.

Responding to a question in parliament, Takaichi suggested that Japan would activate its self-defence force if China attacked Taiwan .

Beijing has since been heaping pressure on Tokyo, from restricting rare earth exports to curbing tourism and even reclaiming its pandas .

Takaichi told parliament earlier this month that she had recorded episodes of Vivant and planned to watch them over the year-end holidays.

State-run Global Times took aim at Sanrio on Wednesday, saying the hugely popular cat character "should not dance with Japan's right wing".

Sanrio "stands to lose far more than short-term sales" by collaborating with "anti-China content", the Global Times article said. "The trust and emotional bond it has built up over a long time will also suffer."

Hello Kitty is not the only internationally beloved figure to have face such wrath in China in recent days.

Earlier this week, several Chinese brands dropped French footballer Kylian Mbappé over comments he had made about late Chinese leader Mao Zedong - which he has since apologised for.

Vivant is about a Japanese salaryman who finds himself entangled in an international web of crime and espionage.

Its first season, which aired in 2023, was set in a fictional Central Asian country. Its second season, which premiered in July, features Chinese agents torturing a Japanese spy by cutting his fingers and stabbing his abdomen.

Chinese state outlets, including CCTV, argued that these tactics "highly overlap" with those historically used by Japanese troops against the Chinese, and that the drama "distorts the truth".

Masamine Ryuho, the president of Vivant's TV network TBS, said on Wednesday that the show was completely fictional and had no intentions of "disparaging any particular country".

articles.title: Spain begins three days of mourning after train crash kills dozens
articles.summary: Emergency teams worked through the night to find victims after one of the worst rail disasters in Europe's modern history.
articles.body:
Spain is beginning three days of mourning after at least 68 people were killed and dozens more were injured in one of the worst rail disasters in Europe's modern history.

Emergency crews worked through the night under powerful floodlights to cut open metal carriages in the search for victims, with many of those killed in the crash still to be identified.

Officials are investigating the cause of the disaster, which occurred when a train travelling from Madrid to Seville barrelled into a stationary train on Wednesday morning.

Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said the "whole of Spain is grieving", adding that "lives have been shattered, families have been torn apart, the pain is immense".

Hundreds of personnel have been deployed to the disaster site to assist with recovery efforts, according to Spain's interior ministry, with drones and helicopters being used to find victims and remove rubble.

The stationary train, run by private rail operator Iryo, had 147 passengers on board, and had stopped on the tracks because of a computer failure, according to Spain's transport minister Óscar Puente.

He said that when there is a system failure, a 24-hour control centre in Madrid takes over, but it had made an "inexplicable" decision to instruct the trains to move again, without any speed restrictions.

Audio recordings between train controllers in Madrid and the train drivers appear to show that one high-speed train was given clearance to move even though another up ahead had stalled.

Iryo said its train was "struck from behind" by another train, run by Spain's state-owned railway company, Renfe, which was carrying 397 passengers. The force of the crash caused several carriages to fall down an embankment.

Witnesses described seeing people crying and bleeding, passengers trapped in their seats and smoke billowing throughout the carriages, one of which caught fire.

Sánchez said it was "unacceptable" that Spain had suffered two serious rail disasters this year, after a high-speed crash killed 46 people near Córdoba in January. It occurred on the same line as Wednesday's accident, but much further south.

Most political parties suspended campaigning for upcoming elections following the incident.

The exception was the far-right party Vox. Its leader, Santiago Abascal, said his party would not take part in what he described as attempts to "use mourning to silence criticism" of the country's rail infrastructure.

Bloodied, dazed and angry - how passengers' rail journey turned to disaster in Spain

What we know so far about deadly Spain train crash

Watch: At the scene of Spain's deadly train crash

Overnight, around 1,500 people gathered outside the Spanish Transport Ministry building in the capital, according to Spanish broadcaster TVE, which reported that demonstrators were largely calling for the resignations of Sánchez and Puente.

Police used tear gas to disperse crowds after protesters hurled bottles and flares. No injuries or arrests were reported.

Rail drivers are expected to go ahead with a planned strike on Thursday, with the Spanish Union of Railway Drivers (Semaf) saying the strike action will be held "in defence of railway safety".

The leader of Spain's main opposition People's Party Alberto Núñez Feijóo said: "Spain has the right to know what is happening with its infrastructure."

Late on Wednesday, relatives were still trying to gather information about passengers who were on either of the trains.

The Spanish Civil Guard has set up bureaus in Madrid, Toledo, Seville and Córdoba to investigate reports of missing persons.

"The top priority is the identification of the missing persons and the taking of DNA samples to be able to locate their relatives," the civil guard wrote in a post on X.

In Toledo, close to the site of the crash, locals observed a minute's silence during a vigil to commemorate the victims.

European Union flags are flying at half-mast in Brussels, in what the European Commission called a "sign of European solidarity" during Spain's mourning period.

Wednesday's crash is the worst the country has seen since 2013, when 80 people died on the outskirts of Santiago de Compostela in north-west Spain.

articles.summary: North Korea fired around a dozen short-range ballistic missiles off its east coast on Thursday, South Korea’s defence ministry said, amid increasing

Seoul has accused North Korea of planting mines south of the military demarcation line, leading to the September 21 explosions. articles.title: 'Fadnavis forced to delete tweet': Congress takes swipe at Maharashtra CM after win in Nagpur MLC polls
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Maharashtra Congress on Thursday took a swipe at chief minister Devendra Fadnavis after the party retained the Nagpur Graduates’
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Maharashtra Congress on Thursday took a swipe at chief minister Devendra Fadnavis after the party retained the Nagpur Graduates’ constituency in the legislative council elections. The final result, which came after more than 40 hours of counting, forced Fadnavis to delete a tweet he had posted the previous day, mocking the Congress for failing to win any seat in the MLC polls.On Wednesday, PM Modi had posted a tweet mocking the Congress for failing to open its account despite the elections being held using ballot papers.The Congress had reacted sharply and dared to hold all elections using ballot papers, asking how many seats the party had won.Congress candidate and sitting MLC Abhijeet Wanjari defeated BJP's Sudhakar Kohale in the Nagpur Graduates’ constituency by 3,271 votes, securing 67,231 votes against his rival's 63,960.Also read -'Commit to ballot paper': Congress dares PM Modi after his 'how many seats' swipe over MLC resultsFadnavis had posted the tweet in response to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s dig at the Congress on X.“By deleting the tweet, Fadnavis has once again preserved Savarkar's legacy! Even before the full results were in hand, in a show of firing a big arrow, Fadnavis tweeted. But that very arrow turned back and pierced straight into his chest! In the end, he was forced to delete the tweet,” the Maharashtra Congress said on X.“Mr. Fadnavis, scared already at this stage? This is just the trailer! In 2029, the people of Maharashtra will drop such a political bombshell on you that even this tweet of today will come back to haunt you! All the best, Mr. Fadnavis! Get ready for the next jolt,” it added.Wanjari, the sitting MLC, secured 67,231 votes against Kohale's 63,960. The result dealt a setback to the BJP in Nagpur, the hometown of Fadnavis and Union minister Nitin Gadkari, both of whom had campaigned extensively for Kohale.Congress hits back at PM Modi over ballot paper remarkThe Congress also targeted Prime Minister Narendra Modi over his remarks on the party's performance in the Legislative Council elections held across four states. Modi had questioned the Congress's tally, pointing out that the polls were conducted using ballot papers."MLC elections in 28 seats across 4 big states - Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Bihar and Karnataka. Elections held using ballot papers. Guess how many seats Congress won?" Modi wrote in a post on X.Congress Rajya Sabha MP Pawan Khera responded by challenging the prime minister to commit to using ballot papers in future Lok Sabha and assembly elections."If Narendra Modi is so confident that EVMs have no bearing on election results, let him prove his confidence in the BJP’s electoral prowess through action, not rhetoric," Khera wrote on X.He also demanded the suspension of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, the restoration of what he alleged were 13.3 crore illegally deleted voters, and action against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.NCP (SP) MLA Rohit Pawar also criticised Fadnavis over the deleted post, pointing to the BJP's defeat in Nagpur, where the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) headquarters is located."Respected Devendra Fadnavis Saheb, In the Nagpur Graduates Constituency, where you yourself took personal interest and went door-to-door to persuade the rebels to withdraw, in that very Nagpur constituency, in the area where the RSS headquarters is located, the BJP had to face defeat—the meaning of this is clear…… It is indeed regrettable that you had to delete your tweet; but the immense ego of power evident in your deleted tweet is not good at all. Anyway, I can understand. Perhaps you forgot that the election was held via ballot, so the tweet might have been made prematurely… Congratulations to the victorious candidate Abhijit Wanjarri, thanks to the graduates who gave their blessings in the form of votes, and best wishes to all the contesting candidates as well!" Pawar wrote on X.MVA wins three of five Maharashtra MLC seatsWith Wanjari's victory, the opposition Maha Vikas Aghadi (MVA) won three of the five Maharashtra Legislative Council seats contested on October 23, while the BJP-led Mahayuti secured two.NCP (SP) candidates Harshada Deshmukh-Jadhav and Pratapsinh Patil won the Pune Graduates’ and Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar Graduates’ constituencies, respectively. Shiv Sena candidate Kiran Sarnaik won the Amravati Teachers’ constituency, while BJP candidate Kaustubh Gawade secured the Pune Teachers’ seat.The Nagpur result followed more than 40 hours of counting. Kohale had led Wanjari after the second round, but neither candidate secured the required quota through first-preference votes. Wanjari eventually overtook his rival during the subsequent elimination rounds as preferential votes were transferred.The outcome dealt a setback to the BJP in a constituency it had traditionally held. Gadkari represented the Nagpur Graduates’ constituency in the Maharashtra Legislative Council for 24 years, from 1990 to 2014.The results have triggered a political exchange between the BJP and opposition parties over electoral performance and the use of electronic voting machines. While Modi cited the ballot-paper polls to question the Congress's performance, the party has used the results to renew its demand for ballot papers in future elections.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: West Virginia farmer let prospectors drill his barren acres in 1906; a gusher reportedly brought him an oil windfall, and he spent $1,500 on a bull his land could not feed
articles.summary: In 1906, a West Virginia farmer leased his barren land to oil drillers, resulting in a $2,000 payout. Discover how this windfall led to the purchase of a $1,500 purebred bull and the intriguing lifestyle changes of rural families in the Appalachian oil boom.
articles.body: During the first decade of the 20th century, gas and oil businesses entered into drilling leases with individual landowners in northern and central parts of West Virginia. Land was granted access to such business entities, which would benefit from the results of drilling, if any. The people familiar with the practice of leasing the lands for drilling in the area of interest were rural families. One such newspaper described how landowners spent their sudden oil windfalls, a topic that attracted public interest at the time.What the December 27, 1906, Bamberg Herald page confirmsAn edition of the Bamberg Herald of December 27, 1906 has been digitised by the University of South Carolina libraries. Under the heading “After Oil Was Struck!” is a story reprinted from a New York paper. The story said that a number of people in West Virginia had become rich because of oil, drilling, and poor farmland. The Bamberg Herald’s copy of the story described the purchase of a bull worth $1,500. The story also mentions a man who wanted a pair of patent leather shoes and a father who bought items with his sons on behalf of their mother. The page doesn’t reveal anything regarding the name of the farmer or the price he got for the gusher. It is said to have been $2,000. However, this isn’t confirmed by the available text of 1906.Appalachian oil output of 35,229,949 barrels in 1897The USGS’s Mineral Resources of the United States, 1897 lists 35,229,949 barrels for the Appalachian field for that year. The report places the Appalachian field across southwest New York, Pennsylvania and West Virginia. Thus, oil was already an established industry in the region, nine years before the 1906 article.West Virginia passes Pennsylvania and reaches an oil production peak of 16 million barrelsWest Virginia’s oil production surpassed Pennsylvania’s in 1898, as the West Virginia Encyclopedia records. In 1906, the year of the newspaper article, the state produced more natural gas than any other state. Sources differ on how long this lead lasted.The encyclopedia puts it at 18 years, which would run to 1924, while the West Virginia Geological and Economic Survey’s history of the state’s mineral industries gives 1906 to 1917, a span of 12 calendar years and a seven-year gap between the two accounts. The survey gives the peak of the state’s oil production as 16 million barrels in 1900, while the encyclopedia dates the same peak to 1901.USGS volume on 1906 mineral resourcesThe USGS lists Mineral Resources of the United States, 1906, written by David T. Day and published in 1907, as the volume in the same annual series that covers the year of the newspaper story. The detail that turned the anecdote into an interesting story was the contrast between the description of the farm that was said to be barren and the $1,500 bull. Whether the farmer bought the bull as an investment in breeding or as a way of showing off is not known. However, the column compared the bull to the shoes and the axe.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 2024, Jason Statham bought a 20-acre English coastal estate for about £20 million; in 2026, a planning rule from 1973 put its two-storey summerhouse under scrutiny over use as guest accommodation
articles.summary: Jason Statham and Rosie Huntington-Whiteley’s plans for a quieter life in the English countryside have encountered an unexpected planning complication.
articles.body: Jason Statham and Rosie Huntington-Whiteley’s plans for a quieter life in the English countryside have encountered an unexpected planning complication. A two-storey summerhouse on the couple’s sprawling Hampshire estate is facing scrutiny over its use as residential accommodation, decades after permission was granted for a very different purpose. According to The Independent and portsmouth, which reported the planning dispute on October 16, 2026, the Hollywood actor has applied for a certificate of lawfulness to establish that the building can continue to be used as accommodation associated with the main house. Planning records from the New Forest National Park Authority identify the application as relating to an existing use, rather than a proposal to create a separate home. The issue centres on a planning condition dating back to February 1973, when the outbuilding was approved as a swimming-pool pavilion, with space for plant and filtration equipment, changing facilities, a sitting room and a small boathouse. Its present-day residential use goes beyond that original purpose.Inside the summerhouse at the Hampshire estateThe building is now configured as a self-contained guest space, with two bedrooms, a bathroom, a fitted kitchen, a dining area and a living room. The application states that these facilities have been in place since at least February 2012, when the property was owned by its previous owners, John and Kim Buckland.The former owners reportedly continued using the summerhouse as residential accommodation after purchasing the estate in 2012 and carried out refurbishment work in late 2018. The planning submission states that the layout has remained unchanged since further refurbishment in 2019. Statham and Huntington-Whiteley acquired the property in March 2024 and have since used the building for visitors, according to the application. The dispute is therefore not about the construction of a new outbuilding, but whether the existing use can be recognised as lawful despite the older planning restriction.The couple are seeking a certificate of lawful development on the grounds that the residential use has continued for more than a decade. The application argues that the length of time involved places the use beyond the period in which planning enforcement action can be taken. That claim remains subject to the planning authority’s assessment of the evidence.A coastal property with extensive groundsThe summerhouse is part of a substantial waterfront estate near Beaulieu, in the New Forest National Park. The property was reportedly purchased for around £20 million, with construction costs estimated at a further £5 million. Its value has also been reported at approximately £25 million.The contemporary, six-bedroom main house was designed by architects Ben Pentreath and Nicholas Umney. Its U-shaped layout wraps around a central courtyard and lap pool, with views across the Solent. The wider grounds include a private beach measuring about 1,200 feet, a lake, stables, a gym, a yoga studio and a large treehouse.The estate’s architecture combines modern planning with traditional materials intended to complement the surrounding coastal woodland. Its secluded setting was reportedly a major attraction for Huntington-Whiteley, who has previously spoken about her longstanding desire to live in the countryside.Previous planning changes at the estateThe summerhouse application follows another planning decision involving the property. In July 2026, Statham secured permission for changes to the driveway and the removal of a small section of the lake to make way for a wildflower meadow. The proposal had prompted ecological concerns about the potential impact on great crested newts.The latest application concerns a separate issue: whether an outbuilding originally approved for leisure-related use can lawfully continue functioning as guest accommodation. It does not seek permission to establish an independent dwelling, and the distinction is important because the summerhouse would remain ancillary to the main house.The New Forest National Park Authority had reportedly indicated during pre-application discussions in March 2025 that the existing use could breach the original planning condition, while also suggesting that the passage of time might be relevant to whether enforcement action remained possible. The authority has yet to determine the certificate application. Until a decision is made, the summerhouse’s existing residential use remains the subject of a planning review, rather than an approved change of use.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: TN govt engages CSIR, NGRI for seismic study of Mullaperiyar dam
articles.summary: Tamil Nadu govt engages CSIR and NGRI to conduct a site-specific seismic study of Mullaperiyar dam as per Supreme Court panel; report due by Dec.
articles.body: Chennai: Tamil Nadu govt has engaged Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) and National Geophysical Research Institute (NGRI), Hyderabad, to conduct a site-specific seismic study of the century-old Mullaperiyar dam.A govt order said the agencies had been engaged under Section 16 of the Tamil Nadu Transparency in Tenders Act, 1998. “The seismic study is being conducted in accordance with directions of the supervisory committee constituted by Supreme Court for monitoring the safety of the dam. Soon, the state will sign an MoU with the agencies,” a senior state govt official said. In 2010, an empowered committee led by former Chief Justice of India A S Anand engaged Pune-based Central Water and Power Research Station to conduct a study on Mullaperiyar.Under the Dam Safety Act, 2021, the first comprehensive safety evaluation of every existing specified dam must be completed within five years of the Act coming into force. Subsequent evaluations are to be conducted at intervals prescribed under the regulations. The evaluation includes a general assessment of seismic safety and, in specified cases, a mandatory study of site-specific seismic parameters.“As Mullaperiyar is an inter-state dam, the report will be submitted to the central comprehensive dam safety evaluation committee before Dec,” the official said. The state govt has maintained that the dam is safe from hydrological, seismic and structural perspectives, citing a 2014 Supreme Court. Keralam govt, however, has continued to demand the construction of a new dam, citing concerns over the safety of people living downstream.In July, Tamil Nadu constituted an independent panel of experts to undertake a comprehensive safety evaluation of 86 dams under the water resources department. The panel of experts from a list empanelled by National Dam Safety Authority, along with serving and retired officials from central and state organisations, will examine aspects such as hydro-mechanical systems, dam design, seismic safety, geology, hydrology and instrumentation. “Further studies will be undertaken based on the evaluation,” an official said.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Chennai | Silver Rate in Chennai | Bank Holidays in Chennai | Public Holidays in Chennai | Chennai AQI | Weather in Chennai | Petrol Price in Chennai | Diesel Price in Chennai | CNG Price in Chennai | LPG Price in ChennaiStay updated with the latest Chennai news.
