articles.title: In 2013, Gerard Butler travelled to Liberia to serve school meals with a charity he supports; it has delivered more than 260 million meals since 2006 and now feeds over 95,000 children every school day
articles.summary: When actor Gerard Butler travelled to Liberia in 2013 to meet children and communities supported by a charity he champions, the visit offered a glimpse
articles.body: When actor Gerard Butler travelled to Liberia in 2013 to meet children and communities supported by a charity he champions, the visit offered a glimpse into how a daily school meal could make a difference in a country recovering from years of conflict. Thirteen years later, that effort has grown into a long-running school feeding programme that has delivered more than 260 million meals to children across Liberia.According to Mary’s Meals, which marked 20 years of its school feeding programme in Liberia in October 2026, more than 95,000 children now receive meals through the charity every school day. The organisation began providing school meals in the country in 2006, building on earlier emergency relief work during and after Liberia’s civil war. Butler, a long-time supporter of the charity, has helped raise awareness of its work through visits to communities in Liberia and Haiti.How a request for food led to a school feeding programmeMary’s Meals’ work in Liberia has roots in the humanitarian response to the country’s civil war. The conflict devastated communities, damaged schools and left many children displaced, hungry and vulnerable. Some children had been recruited as child soldiers, while others had lost their homes and access to education. Father Garry Jenkins, an English priest who had lived in Liberia since 1973 and founded St Dominic’s Catholic School, sought help for children who needed both food and a safe place to learn. When conventional aid channels appeared too slow, he contacted Magnus MacFarlane-Barrow, the founder of the organisation that became Mary’s Meals.MacFarlane-Barrow encouraged him to buy rice in Monrovia, promising to reimburse the cost. The early assistance included food shipments sent under the name Scottish International Relief, the charity’s predecessor. Mary’s Meals later introduced its school feeding programme in Liberia in 2006. The idea was straightforward: provide children with a nutritious meal at school, helping address immediate hunger while encouraging families to send them to class. Over time, the programme developed into a partnership involving schools, local communities, volunteers and supporters.Gerard Butler’s connection with Mary’s MealsButler, the Scottish actor known for films including 300 and Olympus Has Fallen, became involved with Mary’s Meals after presenting its founder, Magnus MacFarlane-Barrow, with a CNN Heroes award in 2010. His support subsequently included visits to Liberia and Haiti, where he met children and communities benefiting from the school feeding programme. The charity said his involvement helped bring international attention to its work and inspired people to support its mission.The award was presented at a ceremony in Berlin on 23 February 2020. Butler described his involvement as a privilege, saying that providing food while children learn was a simple intervention capable of transforming lives. His association with the charity has helped connect its work on the ground with a wider international audience.More than 260 million meals over two decadesMary’s Meals says its programme has provided more than 260 million school meals in Liberia since school feeding began in 2006. The charity now reaches more than 95,000 children every school day, with local volunteers preparing and serving meals in schools. The programme operates across Bong, Bomi, Grand Cape Mount, Gbarpolu and Montserrado counties. Many of the schools it supports are in remote communities, where poor road access can make food deliveries particularly difficult during the rainy season.Rice and peas are among the typical meals served. The organisation aims to source food locally where possible, although supplies sometimes have to be ordered from farther away and well in advance to ensure that schools receive enough food. The charity’s approach links nutrition with education. A meal at school can provide an immediate source of nourishment while giving children and families an additional reason to attend classes regularly. Local volunteers also help keep the programme rooted in the communities it serves.Why the work remains important in LiberiaDespite two decades of school feeding, Liberia continues to face serious challenges linked to poverty, food insecurity and access to education. The country is still dealing with the long-term effects of civil conflict and disease outbreaks, while many communities lack sufficient educational resources. Mary’s Meals says more than half of Liberia’s population lives in poverty and highlights the continuing need to support children who struggle to obtain enough food. The charity’s local partners have also stressed the importance of keeping schools safe and accessible, particularly for children in vulnerable communities. The organisation estimates that £19.15 can provide a child with school meals for an entire year in Liberia and other countries where it operates. Its work now extends to 16 countries, with more than three million children receiving meals every school day worldwide.From emergency food assistance during a period of conflict to a programme serving tens of thousands of children daily, Mary’s Meals has built a sustained presence in Liberia. articles.title: In 1962, Hawaii released Kalij pheasants for hunting; they spread across forests and may have helped disperse seeds of invasive plants such as banana poka
articles.summary: An exploration of how the introduction of Kalij pheasants in Hawaii has contributed to the spread of invasive plants, including banana poka, and its impact on native ecosystems. Discover the ecological implications of this game bird's proliferation through Hawaiian forests.
articles.body: Hawaiian forests evolved in isolation, with their own native plants and birds. They evolved without most of the animals that now share them. In the last hundred years, landowners and wildlife managers have released several birds into Hawaiian forests, mostly to provide hunting opportunities. Some of these released species found favourable conditions in Hawaiian forests and dispersed widely from their initial release areas. Fruit-eating birds may transport seeds long distances through their feces and this is important in forests that are already overgrown with introduced plants. A game bird released for hunting purposes may also have helped spread invasive plants unintentionally. The case of the Kalij pheasant on Hawaii Island illustrates this point.A release of 67 pheasants at Puʻu Waʻawaʻa Ranch in 1962According to Victor and Geraldine Lewin’s 1984 paper in The Wilson Bulletin, kalij pheasants were introduced in 1962 at Puʻu Waʻawaʻa Ranch on Hawaiʻi Island. This introduction was done through an elaborate exotic game bird liberation program conducted by the ranch owners. The Lewins trace the island’s Kalij pheasant population to a single release of 67 birds in 1962, sourced from game farms in Michigan and Texas. The birds remained within the confines of a small silk oak plantation above the release point for about five years.Spread of about 8 km a year across a third of the islandUsing 360 records, the Lewins reconstructed how the species spread across the island. By 1966, the pheasants had moved south around both sides of Mount Hualalai. In 1971, they were already established in the upper Kona Coast above Kailua and in 1972, in the Hilo Forest. The Lewins report an average spread of about 8 km a year, with the birds colonising most of the island’s mid-elevation forest areas within 14 years. By 1984, Kalij pheasants had become widely distributed across various forest types on the island of Hawaii, from sea level to elevations of 2,450 m. Kalij pheasants had already been classified as a legal game species in 1977, seven years before the Lewins documented this wide distribution.Banana poka seeds and fruit in 82% of the 44 pheasants collected in 1981Between January 29 and June 25, 1981, 44 pheasants were caught and dissected for their gizzards and crops. Banana poka seeds and fleshy fruits made up 82% of what the birds ate and the Lewins called it the pheasant’s principal food. Thimbleberry, which is yet another exotic pest plant, showed up in 36%. One gizzard held more than 100 banana poka seeds and more than 3,000 thimbleberry seeds and 63% of the plant foods recorded were exotic. The conservation organisation American Forests notes that banana poka was introduced to Hawaiʻi in the 1920s as an ornamental plant and subsequently spread through forests and fields.What the seed evidence does and does not showThe above study showed many unharmed banana poka and Thimbleberry seeds in the large intestine and feces. In a germination test of 400 thimbleberry seeds kept moist on filter paper, only one seed germinated, a rate of about 0.25%. Because the droppings contained many seeds, the Lewins suggested that the birds may disperse some viable exotic plant material, although the very low germination rate suggests few of those seeds survive. The Lewins also found that pheasants hold banana poka seeds in their gizzards as grit, which wears away the seeds’ hard outer layer, so it is unclear how many of those seeds stay viable.The Lewins conclude that kalij pheasants may be spreading the pest plants and that their presence signals a degraded ecosystem. They warned against moving the pheasants around and recommended that any new stock be free of banana poka.The National Park Service’s account of invasive plant spread in the parkKalij pheasants are commonly seen throughout Hawaiʻi Volcanoes National Park, according to the National Park Service. The agency’s page adds that the birds were released in 1962 and that, because they disperse seeds, their spread has contributed to the spread of invasive plants such as banana poka, thimbleberry and guava. Hawaiʻi Public Radio reports that kalij eat the fruits of banana poka, strawberry guava and clidemia, dispersing the seeds of these plants within native forests.Kalij pheasants implicated as seedling predators in two kipukaA second area of impact is native plants. Technical Report HCSU- 015, released by the University of Hawaii at Hilo in May 2010, was titled Limiting factors of five rare plant species in mesic forests of Hawai'i Volcanoes National Park. According to the U.S. Geological Survey’s summary, scientists studied five rare or endangered native species in Kīpuka Puaulu and Kīpuka Kī over two years. Seed production, rat consumption of the seed and of seedlings, among other factors, was taken into consideration. The report identified kalij pheasants and some unidentified insect species as predators and herbivores of seedlings.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: ‘Does my son know who Harry Potter is?’: Daniel Radcliffe says his son doesn’t recognise him as the famous wizard boy who lived; what the actor’s parenting choice reveals
articles.summary: While the world knows Daniel Radcliffe as the “Boy Who Lived”, his own son has yet to discover that his father is the actor who brought the iconic Harry
articles.body: While the world knows Daniel Radcliffe as the “Boy Who Lived”, his own son has yet to discover that his father is the actor who brought the iconic Harry Potter to life on screen. For millions of fans, the British actor will forever be their magical boy living in Hogwarts, travelling from Platform 9 ¾, and throwing magical spells like Expecto Patronum and the fictional wizard who grew up before their eyes.But at home, Radcliffe is happy to be known by a much simpler title, ‘Dad’.In a candid conversation with The New York Times, the actor revealed that his young son does not yet know that his father played one of the most famous characters in modern cinema. The revelation came after Radcliffe tested his toddler’s recognition of his younger self on a Harry Potter DVD cover and his little boy failed to recognise him.For Radcliffe, it was a moment worth celebrating.“For as long as I can just be his dad, and he won't know me as anything else, I will maintain that for as long as I can,” Radcliffe said. His remarks offer a glimpse into a parenting choice that many families that are famous and successful.The Harry Potter DVD that became a parenting momentHe recalled that someone had given him a DVD to sign. It was lying in his kitchen and his son was standing near it. It was then the actor decided to see if the toddler would recognise the face on the cover.He asked his son who the person was.But his son was clueless and had no idea that the young face on the DVD was no one else but his own father.“Does my son know who Harry Potter is? No, not yet,” the actor said, explaining that he hoped to preserve this separation for as long as possible.Radcliffe and his partner, actress Erin Darke, welcomed their son in April 2023. The couple have kept his name and much of his life away from public eyes, despite Radcliffe himself being grown in front of camera.A child has nothing to do with parent’s fame or celebrity statusFor a child who is still discovering how the world works, a parent's fame may mean very little or nothing at all. The person who is recognised by audiences around the world is, at home, the person who plays, reads stories, answers questions and helps in everyday chores.And Radcliffe looks absolutely happy and content with this. His son knows him for who he is as a person and not as a famous actor yet.Why he is not rushing to introduce his son to Harry PotterRadcliffe is not suggesting that his son must never discover the films. Instead, he appears comfortable allowing that discovery to happen in the child's own time.In his conversation with The New York Times, the actor indicated that he would be happy to read the original Harry Potter books with his son. But only if he is interested. He does not wish to push the franchise on him simply because he played the main character.There is also a practical reason he might prefer his son to watch the forthcoming HBO adaptation of the books rather than the original films. That way, the child could experience the wizarding world without immediately seeing his father playing its central character.A parenting lesson about privacyRadcliffe's parenting approach raises one important question: how much of a parent's identity should shape a child's world?Children discover that their parents have lives outside the home at their own pace. But there is a difference between learning what a parent does and being introduced to the expectations that come with a famous surname.For a celebrity's child, public recognition can bring unwanted attention, comparisons and assumptions before they are old enough to understand them. Keeping family life private can give children more room to develop their own interests and personalities.Fatherhood beyond the fameIn 2023, after his son was born, he described the experience as wonderful while acknowledging how intense and exhausting it could be. He also spoke about wanting to spend time with his family rather than allowing work to consume his life.His comments about keeping his Harry Potter identity from his son fit into that broader picture: fatherhood has given him a role that exists independently of his career.The actor became internationally famous as a child himself, playing Harry Potter across eight films. But his son has yet to discover that. Until then, Radcliffe is enjoying a phase that fame cannot give him. For millions of fans, Daniel Radcliffe will always be the boy who received his Hogwarts letter. But for his son, at least for now, he is just Dad. And that, it seems, is precisely how the actor wants it.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ testGet the latest Lifestyle News and more. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: DMK seeks Presidential reference to SC on SIR deletions
articles.summary: DMK chief M K Stalin urges President Murmu to seek SC opinion on deleting 97 lakh voters in TN SIR, alleges poll manipulation, seeks audit and action on CEC.
articles.body: Chennai: DMK president M K Stalin has urged President Droupadi Murmu to make a Presidential reference to Supreme Court under Article 143 of the Constitution, seeking its opinion on the validity of deleting 97 lakh names from Tamil Nadu’s electoral rolls during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR).In a 19-page memorandum, Stalin also sought a Presidential reference to Parliament under Article 86(2) for initiating action against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. He accused Kumar of taking “illegal, unilateral, and unconstitutional” decisions by overriding the views of the other two election commissioners.Stalin said the deletions had disproportionately affected constituencies considered strongholds of DMK and alleged that the exercise had influenced the outcome of the assembly election. TVK won a larger share of seats where deletions were higher, he said.Noting that DMK’s objections were not an afterthought prompted by the election results, Stalin said he had opposed the exercise while serving as chief minister and had also raised concerns when reports emerged of large-scale and targeted deletion of voters in Bihar in 2025.He sought a direction to ECI that the “tainted post-SIR roll” not be used for any future election or by-election and that the pre-SIR roll be restored, besides an independent forensic audit of the ECINET and ERONET systems. He called for measures to restore public confidence in the electoral process, including the conduct of elections through paper ballots and counting of 100% of VVPAT slips pending such a change. The memorandum follows decisions taken by DMK MPs at a meeting chaired by Stalin on Oct 17.“This is the first and largest scam the country has ever witnessed, perpetrated by the CEC, breaching the constitutional faith and trust reposed in him,” Stalin said. Party sources said the memorandum was sent by email after a DMK delegation could not get an appointment with President till Wednesday.“The election result in Kolathur was manipulated by deleting a large number of voters without reason to ensure that I did not win the election. These motivated deletions tilted the result in favour of the newly floated TVK,” Stalin said, expressing shock over the deletion of one lakh electors in Kolathur. He cited Tirupattur, Kanyakumari, Polur, Tirukkoilur and Paramathi-Velur, where the results were decided by narrow margins.DMK booth-level agents had assisted voters in enrolling during the SIR exercise.
